'''''Forsythia ''×'' intermedia''''', or '''border forsythia,'''<ref name=Dirr>{{cite book|author=Dirr, Michael A.| title=Dirr's Hardy Trees and Shrubs - An Illustrated Encyclopedia| publisher=Timber Press|page=58 | year=1997 | isbn=978-0-88192-404-6|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=CmKi3t5qZe4C&pg=PA158&dq=Forsythia%20xintermedia| accessdate=2009-06-02}}</ref> is an ornamental deciduous [[shrub]] of garden origin.

==Description==
[[File:Forsythia x intermedia 0zz.jpg|thumb]]
The shrub has an upright habit with arching branches and grows to 3 to 4 metres high.<ref name=Rowell>{{cite book|author=Rowell, Raymond J.| title=Ornamental Flowering Trees in Australia| publisher=AH & AW Reed Pty Ltd.|location=Australia | year=1980 | isbn=978-0-589-50178-5}}</ref>  The opposite leaves turn yellowish or occasionally purplish in the autumn before falling.<ref name=NYSU>{{cite web|title=''Forsythia x intermedia''|work=Plant fact sheets|publisher=NC State University|url=http://www.ces.ncsu.edu/depts/hort/consumer/factsheets/shrubs/forsythia_xintermedia.html|accessdate=2009-06-01|archive-date=2009-03-29|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090329060718/http://www.ces.ncsu.edu/depts/hort/consumer/factsheets/shrubs/forsythia_xintermedia.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> The bright yellow flowers are produced on one- to two-year-old growth and may be solitary or in racemes from 2 to 6.<ref name = Rowell/>

==Origin==
The hybrid is thought to be a cross between ''[[Forsythia viridissima]]'' and [[Forsythia suspensa|''F. suspensa'' var. ''fortunei'']].<ref name=INRA/> A plant of seedling origin was discovered growing in the  [[Alter Botanischer Garten der Universität Göttingen|Göttingen Botanical Garden]] in Germany by the director of the Royal Prussian Academy of Forestry in [[Münden]], H. Zabel in 1878.<ref name=INRA>{{cite web|title=''Forsythia x intermedia''|publisher=INRA Centre d'Angers|url=http://www.inra.fr/internet/Produits/WEBTEXTO/angers/forsythia/variet/1.html|accessdate=2009-06-02}}</ref> Zabel formally described and named the hybrid  in ''[[Gartenflora]]'' in 1885.<ref name=GRIN>{{GRIN | accessdate=2009-06-02}}</ref> It was introduced to the [[Arnold Arboretum]] in the United States in 1889.<ref Name=INRA/>

==Cultivation==
The hybrid is best suited to a position in full sun or partial shade and is drought-tolerant.<ref name=NYSU/> Like some other forsythias it is one of the earliest shrubs to flower. Well adapted to temperature changes, it blooms with bright yellow flowers that are noticeable even in [[twilight]]. It is one of several forsythia species that are widely cultivated in gardens and parks.

==Chemistry==
The first [[dirigent protein]] was discovered in ''Forsythia intermedia''. This protein has been found to direct the [[stereoselective biosynthesis]] of (+)-[[pinoresinol]] from [[coniferyl alcohol]] monomers.<ref>{{cite journal |vauthors=Davin LB, Wang HB, Crowell AL |title=Stereoselective bimolecular phenoxy radical coupling by an auxiliary (dirigent) protein without an active center |journal=Science |volume=275 |issue=5298 |pages=362–6 |year=1997 |pmid=8994027 |doi=10.1126/science.275.5298.362|display-authors=etal}}</ref>
